memory_candidates.content: When auditing a directory-pathspec-to-explicit-list migration (e.g. task 309's stage_paths[] accumulator replacing a bare `-- specs/` token), check every rename/move call site the migration touched for whether BOTH the old and new path were preserved. A directory token silently covers both sides of a rename; an explicit list only covers what it is told, so the migration's predictable blind spot is an omitted vacated-source path at each mv site it converted. Grep `git log -S '<the exact stage_paths literal>'` to find the introducing commit precisely.

lint-directory-pathspec-boundary.sh and git-commit-scoped.sh's V2/V5/V6 gates are all structurally blind to an OMITTED pathspec token (too-narrow list), as opposed to a too-WIDE bare directory token. The lint's Layer 2 classifier only flags tokens that are present and end in `/` with no task-scoped component; the V2/V5/V6 gates only ever inspect pathspecs they are given. A missing rename endpoint is therefore invisible to every existing staging gate and fails silently (commit exits 0, `create mode` only, vacated source left as an unstaged ` D`).
